messages.content:
Return only the deliverable. Use short, plain, complete sentences. Lead with the answer. A memo is a short standalone paragraph, not a form: add no heading, subject line, label, preface or conclusion. Say each fact once. Aim for 60–80 words from a long source, but keep all facts even if that needs more words.

Meaning comes before length. Preserve every unique source fact: results, limits, exclusions, unknowns, evidence, owners, next actions and prerequisites. Copy technical strings character for character, including spaces and hyphens. Preserve negations, numbers, units, commands, errors, filenames, fields, frontmatter and code blocks. Never invent or infer a completed action.

Copy an already concise source EXACTLY, with no added words. Return requested JSON alone with exact keys and types. Explicit requests for detail override brevity: include ordered steps, reasons, conditions and provenance. Check the final text against every source sentence for missing information.

Existing memo rewrites require an explicit request, preview and approved save through validated memo.write with expected_revision. Stop on conflict; preserve newer text, source transcripts and detailed evidence. Draft in one normal model call.

Write the requested deliverable from the supplied source. Preserve every substantive fact, constraint, uncertainty, provenance and next action. Do not invent information. Return only the deliverable, with no account of your editing process.

Deliverable surface: memo.
Write a concise standalone API migration note.

Source:
This note should explain the change to the pagination response and should preserve the compatibility details rather than merely saying that pagination was improved. Version 2 adds the next_cursor field. Version 1 clients continue to receive their existing items field, and that field is not being removed. A null next_cursor means that the captured result has no further page. Results are captured once for a query. Files created after that capture do not appear in later pages of the same result. A caller that needs current files must start a new query instead of expecting the cursor to refresh the tree. Cursor state expires when the run is retired. These decisions are specified in api-pagination-2, which is the evidence reference for the migration. The next action is to update the client example so that it follows next_cursor until it is null. There is no change to write permissions or file ownership as part of this API change.

message.content: The API now returns a next_cursor field in pagination responses (v2). Version 1 clients still receive the items field, which remains unchanged. A null next_cursor indicates no further pages. Results are captured once per query; files added after capture do not appear in later pages of that result. To see current files, start a new query instead of relying on the cursor. Cursor state expires when the run is retired. Update client examples to follow next_cursor until null. No changes to write permissions or file ownership.
